findings: Both captures document Payment Element and SetupIntent saving without a purchase for Bimpli, Pluxee and Up Déjeuner in private preview. November explicitly adds the waitlist, preview Stripe API version 2026-05-27.preview or later, a per-restaurant/store PaymentLocation set up through the API and an active fr_meal_vouchers_conecs_payments capability. Preview access, location capability and payment-method eligibility are distinct requirements (new raw lines 5-37).

Server SetupIntent creation takes Customer ID, setup_details[location] and setup_details[benefit][fr_meal_voucher][enabled]=if_payment_method_is_eligible. The server sends only the SetupIntent client secret to the client. Payment Element supplies the details to stripe.confirmSetup with a return_url. A later on-session payment, while the customer is present and can authenticate, takes Customer and saved PaymentMethod IDs, EUR, payment_details[location] and the matching payment_details eligibility field in a separate server PaymentIntent. The example requests confirmation with confirm=true. An active location, a return URL and a confirmation request alone establish neither eligible classification nor successful authorization, capture or settlement (new raw lines 35-71).

November's sandbox keeps the Bimpli with Conecs test card, any three-digit CVC and any future expiration, but uses a PaymentLocation ID from onboarding in that same sandbox. Both captures describe possible issuer verification during saving, reflected as a temporary EUR 0.30 statement entry that Stripe reverses almost immediately and restores to the daily balance. This is conditional card verification, distinct from a completed voucher purchase or refund (old raw lines 75-92, new raw lines 73-85).

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-saving-payment-details-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-fr-meal-vouchers-save-payment-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-fr-meal-vouchers-save-payment.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/meal-vouchers/fr-meal-vouchers/saving-payment-details`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/meal-vouchers/fr-meal-vouchers/saving-payment-details, November documents saving French meal vouchers for Bimpli, Pluxee and Up Déjeuner in private preview. It requires Stripe API version 2026-05-27.preview or later and an API-onboarded PaymentLocation with active fr_meal_vouchers_conecs_payments. The server creates a SetupIntent with Customer ID, setup_details[location] and setup_details[benefit][fr_meal_voucher][enabled]=if_payment_method_is_eligible, then passes the client secret to Payment Element's stripe.confirmSetup flow with return_url. Before reuse, verify that SetupIntent succeeded and identify its saved PaymentMethod. The April 21 general Elements save guide shows looking up the SetupIntent via stripe.retrieveSetupIntent with its client secret, checking its status, and finding the resulting payment_method saved to the Customer on success. The November Stripe.js reference corroborates lookup by client secret (raw/stripe-save-and-reuse-elements-2025.md:946-953,967-986 and raw/stripe-js-setup-intents-retrieve-setup-intent-2026-11-07.md:5-12). This companion guidance distinguishes arrival at return_url from successful setup or a purchase. The meal voucher's SetupIntent handoff and saved-method reuse are in old raw lines 50-62 and new raw lines 47-57. A later on-session EUR charge uses a separate PaymentIntent, Customer and saved PaymentMethod IDs, payment_details[location], the corresponding eligibility flag and confirm=true in the example. Sandbox setup takes a location ID from the same sandbox. An issuer verification may appear as a temporary 0.30 EUR authorization that is reversed almost immediately (new raw lines 9-51 and new raw lines 53-85). The May 5 capture and source-stripe-fr-meal-vouchers-save-payment.md use a pre-provisioned SIRET in each intent and older test SIRET examples. They share the SetupIntent versus on-session PaymentIntent split, EUR, test card and conditional authorization behavior (old raw lines 19-54 and old raw lines 56-92).
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/meal-vouchers/fr-meal-vouchers/saving-payment-details, the preview access and version terms, active per-location capability, location and eligibility parameters on both intents, and sandbox input are substantive (new raw lines 9-44 and new raw lines 53-81). The Node-to-curl switch and Elements variant banner removal are presentational. Date the May direct-SIRET setup and payment parameters and provisioned/invalid test SIRETs in source-stripe-fr-meal-vouchers-save-payment.md (old raw lines 19-54 and old raw lines 56-92). Cross-link the two contracts and distinguish the preview location's registered SIRET and possible onboarding review from the older Dashboard-managed record. Keep the companion accept-payment CVC and PaymentIntent SIRET-at-confirmation claims specific to that path. Both new curl samples omit Stripe-Version (new raw lines 39-45 and new raw lines 61-71), so a raw HTTP request as shown uses the account's default API version (raw/stripe-sdks-set-version-2026-11-07.md:5-17). Actually select 2026-05-27.preview or a later supported preview version (new raw lines 25-29). When the account default does not meet that requirement, use an explicit Stripe-Version header for those HTTP requests. Version selection establishes neither a particular SDK release nor preview entitlement. The client receives the SetupIntent client secret, while server requests use the secret key. A waitlist request, location activation, client redirect and conditional verification do not establish a successful purchase, capture, settlement or off-session eligibility.
